paper_metadata.title: Tailoring the deformation mechanisms in a Ni-Co-based superalloy by controlling γ′ precipitate size

evidence.quote: This study investigates the deformation mechanisms in a Ni-Co-based superalloy with γ′ precipitates varying from 31 to 122 nm under two compression conditions at 760 ◦C.
The chemical composition of the experimental Ni-Co-based superalloy is 25.0 Co, 10.0 Cr, 4.0 Mo, 1.5 W, 4.5 Ti, 2.3 Al, 0.7 Nb, and 52.0 Ni (wt. %).

mechanisms.name: particle shearing by strong dislocation coupling pairs

evidence.quote: it is evident that in A0, the CRSSs of strong dislocation coupling pairs and SFs were similar around the γ′ size of 31 nm, hence both were observed.

mechanisms.name: stacking fault formation by partial dislocation decomposition

evidence.quote: To reduce the stress of the interface and the energy of the structure, the isolated SFs (Fig. 2a) form when some a/2〈101〉 dislocations cut into the precipitates and decompose into two partial a/3〈112〉 and a/6〈121〉 dislocations [11].
As a result, the dislocations tended to bypass the γ′ precipitates to form Orowan loops, and only some dislocations cut through the precipitated phase to produce the isolated SFs [13].

mechanisms.name: micro-twin formation by thermally driven atomic rearrangement

evidence.quote: In A24, the low CRSS of SFs favored the generation of high-density SFs, leading to the formation of MTs under the influence of thermal activation (Fig. 2e) [12].

mechanisms.name: micro-twin formation by high external stress and defect accumulation

evidence.quote: However, in the 20 % strain samples, the applied high external stress is sufficient to reach the CRSS for continuous SF formation. Additionally, the larger deformation leads to the generation of more defects, facilitating atomic rearrangements to form MTs [12].
